summary: You present a worthwhile Australian coral-monitoring mission, identify marine and conservation scientists as users, and provide a useful project timetable and initial STK learning. To reach the next rubric level, turn the broad concept into measurable mission requirements, add and interpret preliminary engineering results, strengthen contingency planning, and polish citations and writing.
next_steps: In “Mission Concept & Rationale,” define a candidate sensor and measurable requirements for coverage, revisit interval, data delivery and orbit. Explain how the cited Hawaii reef-mapping work could translate to a spaceborne instrument, including feasibility.

Build on Image 1 with specific milestones, decision points and contingency time. Connect each task to the mission design, and identify how you will adjust the plan if launch/orbit options or technical assumptions change.

Use your STK tutorial work to produce and briefly interpret an initial design result, such as a candidate orbit or coverage analysis. Include the assumptions and explain what the result means for monitoring the Great Barrier Reef.

criteria.C1: In “Mission Concept & Rationale,” you identify a relevant Australian need, marine and conservation scientists as users, and the intended monitoring benefit. For the next level, define measurable objectives and requirements, including sensor performance, coverage, revisit and data delivery, and establish how airborne reef-mapping methods could work from orbit.
criteria.C2: Image 1 gives you a timetable, and your plan covers research, launch, orbit, communications, STK and editing; “Useful Links” identifies planned sources. To reach the next level, add specific deliverables and decision milestones, explain how the schedule serves the mission, and include contingency time or alternative actions.
criteria.C3: You have completed background research and STK tutorials 1–4, which are useful preparation. To reach the next level, present preliminary technical results—such as an orbit, coverage or payload analysis—and briefly interpret them against the mission needs.
criteria.C4: Your headings provide a logical structure, and Image 1 is labelled and readable. To reach the next level, refine awkward phrasing and make the presentation consistent; replace bare URLs in “Useful Links” with complete, consistently formatted references and ensure in-text citations match the reference list.
